findings.title: Secret in hardcoded local value
findings.description: A Terraform local with a secret-like name (password, secret, token) and a hardcoded string value bakes the credential into version control and state. Reference a secrets manager instead. The secret value is never included in findings.
findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded secret immediately and rotate it. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) and reference them via data sources. Never commit secrets to version control — scan history with gitleaks if the value was ever committed.

findings.title: SNS topic using AWS-managed encryption key
findings.description: A topic with kms_master_key_id explicitly set to alias/aws/sns encrypts with the AWS-managed key, which the account cannot rotate or control via key policy. Consider a customer-managed key for full key control. (Missing kms_master_key_id is AEGIS-AWS-341.)
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: SNS topic without display name
findings.description: A topic with no display_name is harder to identify in notifications and audit trails. Set a human-readable display name for every topic.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.
